newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada rejects "fast track" satellite TV bids.
newsitem.headline: Canada rejects "fast track" satellite TV bids.

text.p: Industry Canada said on Tuesday it rejected "fast track" licensing proposals from Telesat Canada and Borealis Space Corp for the operation of two satellites in Canadian orbital slots for direct broadcast television.

"Proposals submitted by Borealis Space Corp and Telesat Canada to provide a Canadian DBS (direct broadcast satellite) facility did not meet the rigorous "fast track" criteria," the department said in a statement.
In November, Canadian companies were given a February 28 deadline to submit their satellite proposals.

But companies that already had direct broadcast (DBS) satellites or sufficient DBS capacity to meet interim Canadian needs were given until December 16 to apply for "fast track" licensing. Telesat and Borealis were the only two applicants in the "fast track" category.

Telesat said it would submit a new proposal on February 28. "As we've demonstrated time and again since we first proposed direct-to-home (DTH) service in 1985, Telesat will spare no effort in developing a plan that will bring Canadians DTH television," Telesat chief executive Larry Boisvert said in a statement.

Industry Canada's decision to invite Canadian-only bids for the use of the satellite slots came after the U.S. Federal Communications Commission denied a bid by Telquest Ventures and Tele-Communications Inc to beam TV programs across North America using two Canadian satellites that were to be owned and operated by Telesat.
Telesat is 95 percent-owned by Stentor, the telephone consortium led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada and five percent by Toronto-based Spar Aerospace Ltd.
